newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Zaire rebels aim to topple Mobutu - leader.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels aim to topple Mobutu - leader.

text.p: The commander of rebels fighting Zairean troops in the east of the country said his multi-ethnic force would not stop after gaining control of three towns and aimed to topple Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seke.

Andre Kissasse Ngandu was also quoted as saying he was opposed to the idea, proposed by France and Spain, of an international military force to ensure aid gets to thousands of refugees fleeing ethnic conflict in Zaire.

"Our goal is to overthrow the regime in Kinshasha and all it stands for...corruption, misery for the people," Ngandu, military head of the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, told the daily Libre Belgique.
Speaking from the eastern Zaire city of Goma, Ngandu said: "It is not a matter of persons -- i.e. President Mobutu -- but of a will for change."
"Now we are in control of Goma, Bukavu and Uvira and we will go to Kinshasha if need be."

Asked if the alliance would team up with legal opposition parties such as the UDPS, he said: "Why not...we are in touch with other anti-Mobutu forces in Zaire...they (the UDPS) are no different from us. After six years of a Mobutu-style "multi'-party state we have opted for armed struggle."
The paper quoted Rubens Mikindo of the North Kivu UDPS as saying he wished to "sit at the same table as the rebels."

After declaring his opposition to the idea of an international intervention force to ensure aid gets through, Ngandu said: "We would protect refugees, guarantee aid for them and allow them to choose between exile and voluntary return."
